t_advice_summary_textbox.text: The color of the gnome hats is not related to outcome. Instead gnomes with short hats are more likely to give higher scores. The time allotted makes it difficult to behave as though it is anything other than a game of chance. Trusting your instincts is probably sufficient.

vb_textbox.text: Gnomes come in distinct sets of 2 that are always present together. One of the gnomes will consistently give more mushrooms than the other. Which can be figured out after one or two trials. This is tricky to explain, but there appear to be at least 2 different sets of configurations for the gnomes presented. So for some number of turns (50 for example) there will be 3 options (red vs green, orange vs pink, and red vs brown). At some random interval the gnomes presented will change. While the red and green pair will still appear the higher value gnome will be different. Some sets such as the orange vs pink will stop appearing and a new color combanation such as blue vs yellow will appear. When you start to see a combination that has not appeared in many turns it is time to test and find out if the higher value gnome has changed with a few rounds of testing each combo. Due to the speed of the game I am unsure if the higher value gnome is always the same for each configuration, but I think that it is. Thus once you figure each configuration out it is fairly easy to figure out when the configuration has switched and adjust accordingly. Some bad rounds are inevitable, but it is possible to get a generally high score with this strategy.
